paper.title: Hybrid Combinatorial Multi-armed Bandits with Probabilistically Triggered Arms

unmapped: Learner is given an offline dataset with N_i i.i.d. samples per base arm from an offline distribution whose means may differ from online means
Learner knows a bias-control vector V with |mu_i^off - mu_i^on| <= V_i
Reward satisfies monotonicity and 1-norm TPM bounded smoothness with constant B
Access to an offline (alpha,beta)-approximation oracle taking mean vectors as input; regret is (alpha,beta)-approximation regret
settings.definition_quote: The online environment consists of $m$ base arms, represented as random variables $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_m$, jointly distributed according to an unknown distribution $D^\text{on} \in \mathcal{D}$, where $D^\text{on}$ is supported on $[0,1]^m$ ... the key difference between H-CMAB-T and CMAB-T problem is that before online learning, the player is given an offline data collection $\mathcal{B}$. ... $|\mu_i^{\text{off}} - \mu_i^{\text{on}}| \leq V_i$

symbols.K_trig: max number of arms that can be triggered by an action (paper's K)
symbols.Delta_min_i: minimum positive action gap among actions that can trigger arm i
symbols.N_i_prime: effective offline sample count N_i*max{1-2B K omega_i/Delta_min_i,0}^2
symbols.N_i: number of offline samples of arm i

conditions: 1-norm TPM bounded smoothness with constant B (Condition 2)

source.label: thm:regret-bound
source.quote: For an H-CMAB-T problem ... that satisfies monotonicity (Condition~1) and TPM bounded smoothness (Condition~2), the hybrid CUCB algorithm with an input bias control vector $V$ and an $(\alpha, \beta)$-approximation oracle achieves an $(\alpha, \beta)$-approximate gap-dependent regret bounded by: \sum_{i \in [m]} \max\{ \frac{64 \sqrt{2} B^2 K \log(4mT^3)}{\Delta_{\min}^i} - 8B \sqrt{2N_i' \log(4mT^3)}, 0 \} + 4Bm + \frac{\pi^2}{6}\Delta_{\max}

results.notes: Regret is (alpha,beta)-approximation regret defined via expected rewards r_S(mu). Delta_max here is max over arms of Delta_max^i (action gaps). Recovers CUCB bound of Wang & Chen 2017 when N_i'=0. Polynomial compute assuming oracle.

symbols.K_trig: max number of triggerable arms per action (paper's K)
symbols.tau_star: optimal value of LP max tau s.t. tau <= N_i + n(i), sum n(i) <= KT

source.label: thm:gap-indep
source.quote: the hybrid CUCB algorithm with an input bias control vector $V$ and an $(\alpha, \beta)$-approximation oracle achieves an $(\alpha, \beta)$-approximate gap-independent regret bounded by: \min\{ \psi, \gamma \} +4Bm + \frac{\pi^2}{6}\Delta_{\max}

results.notes: Contains Delta_max (instance quantity) though called gap-independent. Appendix proof's final line has 16BT rather than 16BKT; recorded as stated in theorem.

symbols.Delta_min_i: min action gap for arm i
symbols.N_i_dprime: N_i*min{1 - B omega_i/(K Delta_min_i), 0}^2 as written in paper

conditions: specific hard instance: actions of size K, exactly one arm triggered uniformly, Bernoulli outcomes, linear reward (B/K) sum mu_j

source.quote: Reg(T) = \sum_{i \in [m]} Reg_i(T) \ge B\sum_{i \in[m]}( \frac{K\log T}{B\Delta^i_{\min}} - \sqrt{N_i^{\prime\prime} \cdot \log T}), where N_i''=N_i\min\{1-\frac{B\omega_i}{K\Delta^i_{\min}},0\}^2.

results.notes: Informal derivation, not a numbered theorem; uses ≳ and has apparent typos (min vs max). Algorithm class for lower bound is implicitly consistent algorithms (log T lower bound).
